title: Compact singular-continuous Cantor primitive inside the positive holonomy class

cantor_class.construction: For the middle-thirds Cantor distribution F_C and a>1, set G_a(x)=F_C(x)-F_C(x-a).
cantor_class.compact_bv: G_a is compactly supported in [0,1+a], continuous, and of bounded variation.
cantor_class.derivative: DG_a=mu_C-tau_a mu_C is atom-free and purely singular continuous with total mass zero.
cantor_class.holder: F_C and G_a are Holder with alpha=log(2)/log(3).
cantor_class.fractional_membership: Monotonicity and Holder continuity make the squared L2 increment O(|h|^(1+alpha)), so the difference-quotient characterization gives G_a in H^s(R) for every s<(1+log(2)/log(3))/2, including s=3/4.
cantor_class.holonomy: K1633 therefore gives widehat G_a in L1 for an explicit compact primitive with singular-continuous derivative.
cantor_class.scope_guard: This is a positive singular-continuous subclass. It does not prove that every atom-free singular derivative measure yields Fourier/holonomy L1.
